pages.desc: Free house cleaning price calculator. Enter your pay goal, hours and costs to get your break-even rate, your target rate and a quote for any clean, drive time included.
pages.lede: Find what a clean has to cost so it pays you: your break-even rate, your target rate and a quote for the job, with drive time and self-employment tax counted. Free, no sign-up.
pages.card: Break-even rate, target rate and a quote for any clean, drive time included.
pages.costs_hint: Insurance, phone, apps, marketing, equipment, fees
method: Most cleaners divide the pay they want by the hours they work. That leaves out three things: the hours nobody pays for (driving, quoting, invoicing), the business costs that run every month, and self-employment tax.

This calculator grosses your take-home up for self-employment tax (15.3% on 92.35% of profit) and your income tax estimate, adds a year of business costs, and spreads the total over the hours customers actually pay for. That is your break-even rate. Your margin on top gives the target rate.
A job's price floor is your time on site and your drive time at the break-even rate, plus vehicle cost per mile and supplies. The quote adds your margin and rounds up to the next $5.
pages.example: A $52,000 take-home goal with a 12% income tax estimate needs $70,394 of profit before tax. Add $6,540 a year of business costs and you need $76,934 of revenue. At 48 weeks of 45 hours with 65% paid, that is 1,404 paid hours: a break-even rate of $54.80 and a target of $64.47 with a 15% margin. Pay divided by all hours would say $24.07. A standard 2-bed clean (2.5 hours on site, a 15-mile round trip, $8 of supplies) has a $183.79 price floor and quotes at $220, with $36.21 of profit inside it.

faq: How much should I charge to clean a house?

There is no single right price, because it depends on your pay goal, your costs and how many of your hours customers pay for. Enter yours above and the calculator shows the lowest price that covers them and a quote with your margin.
Why is my break-even rate so much higher than my pay divided by my hours?

Because part of every week is unpaid (driving, quoting, admin), your business costs keep running, and as a self-employed cleaner you pay both halves of Social Security and Medicare. Each of those raises the rate every paid hour has to carry.
Does it work for deep cleans and move-outs?
Yes. Pick an example job or type your own hours, crew size, supplies and miles. The example jobs are starting points, not market prices.
Is this tax advice?
No. It is a planning estimate. Ask your tax preparer for your real income tax rate.

pages.title: 13 Week Cash Flow Calculator for Ecommerce | ProofNotFluff
pages.desc: Free 13 week cash flow calculator for ecommerce brands. Enter cash today, weekly payouts, weekly costs and one purchase order to see your lowest cash week and the cash you need to cover it.
pages.h1: 13 Week Cash Flow Calculator for Ecommerce
pages.lede: See the week your cash bottoms out and how much you need to cover it, before a purchase order lands. Free, no sign-up.
pages.card: Your lowest cash week in the next 13, and the cash needed to cover it.
method: Each week starts with last week's ending cash, adds the payouts that reach your bank and takes out your fixed costs and ad spend. In the week the purchase order is due, its payment comes out too.
The lowest ending cash across the 13 weeks is your low point. If it is below zero, the cash needed is the amount that keeps that week at zero.

This free version uses one weekly figure for cash in and one purchase order paid in a single week. Real brands wait days or weeks for each channel to pay out and pay POs as a deposit and a balance; the full workbook models both.
pages.example: Say a brand starts with $20,000 and collects $53,700 a week after fees while paying $32,000 a week in payroll, fixed costs and ads. That adds $21,700 a week, so cash reaches $85,100 by week 3. A $117,000 PO balance due in week 4 takes it to -$10,200, so the brand needs $10,200 more by then, or a later due date. By week 13 cash is back to $185,100. The weekly figures are the week 1 numbers from example 1 of the 13-Week E-commerce Cash Flow workbook; the starting cash and due week are changed to show a squeeze.

cta.title: The full 13-week cash flow
bullets: The 13-Week E-commerce Cash Flow workbook models each channel's payout lag (Amazon, TikTok Shop, your own store, retail), up to six POs as deposit plus balance and freight,
factoring cost in dollars, a credit line, side-by-side scenarios and a PO planner, for Excel and Google Sheets.

faq: What is a 13 week cash flow?
A week-by-week plan of the cash coming in and going out over the next quarter, so you can see the lowest week before it happens. Thirteen weeks is one quarter.
Why can a profitable store run out of cash?
Sales are recorded when they happen, but payouts arrive later and inventory is paid for before it sells. Growing sales and big purchase orders widen that gap.
Should I use sales or payouts for cash in?
Payouts: the money that reaches your bank after fees and refunds, in the week it arrives.
What if the lowest week is below zero?
You need that much cash, credit or a later payment date by that week. Moving a PO's due date is often the first lever to test.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is a planning estimate based on the numbers you enter.

pages.title: Etsy Fee Calculator: Fees, Payout and Profit per Sale | ProofNotFluff
pages.desc: Free Etsy fee calculator for US sellers. Enter your price, shipping and costs to see the transaction fee, payment processing, listing fee, Offsite Ads, your payout and your profit on one sale.
pages.lede: See every Etsy fee on one sale, what Etsy pays you, and what you keep after your costs. With or without an Offsite Ads order. Free, no sign-up.
pages.card: Every Etsy fee on one sale, your payout and your profit, Offsite Ads included.
ads_options: Yes: 15% (shop under $10,000 in sales over 365 days)

asof.tail: Every rate is editable if Etsy changes one.

method: Etsy charges a 6.5% transaction fee on the item price plus the shipping you charge, but not on US sales tax. Payment processing for a US bank account is 3% of everything the buyer paid, sales tax included, plus $0.25 an order. Each sale also carries a $0.20 listing fee, because a listing with more than one in stock renews for $0.20 after each sale.

If Etsy attributes the order to one of its Offsite Ads, it adds 15% of the item price plus shipping, or 12% once a shop has made $10,000 or more in sales over the prior 365 days. That fee never goes over $100 on one order.

Each fee is rounded to the cent. What is left after the fees is your payout. Take away the item cost and the shipping label and you have the profit on the sale. Margin is that profit divided by the item price plus shipping.
pages.example: Take an 8 oz soy candle listed at $24 with $5.50 shipping charged, $10.20 of materials, packaging and making time, and a $6.25 label. Etsy's fees come to $3.26: $1.92 transaction fee, $1.14 payment processing and the $0.20 listing fee. Etsy pays out $26.24 and the sale makes $9.79, a 33.2% margin. If the same order came through an Offsite Ad at 15%, another $4.43 comes off and profit drops to $5.36. These are the inputs for the 8 oz candle in the example shop inside the True Profit System for Etsy Sellers workbook, which shows $9.80 because it does not round each fee to the cent.

cta.title: Every listing, every order, every payout
bullets: The True Profit System for Etsy Sellers workbook uses this same maths for Excel and Google Sheets:
true profit and an OK, WATCH or REPRICE flag on every listing, the list price that hits the profit you want, an order log, a payout check to the cent and a tax reserve. $2.99, instant download.

faq: What fees does Etsy take from a sale?

For a US seller: a 6.5% transaction fee on the item price plus shipping, payment processing of 3% plus $0.25 on the total the buyer paid, and a $0.20 listing fee. Orders Etsy attributes to Offsite Ads add 15% or 12%, up to $100.
Does Etsy charge fees on shipping?
Yes. The transaction fee and payment processing both apply to the shipping you charge, so moving shipping into the item price does not change those two fees.
Why is a listing fee counted on every sale?
A listing costs $0.20 to publish, and a listing with more than one in stock renews for another $0.20 after each sale. So each sale carries one listing fee.
I sell from outside the US. Does this work?
Yes, if you type your own rates. Etsy's payment processing fee depends on the country of your bank account.
Is this tax or financial advice?
No. It is a planning estimate based on the numbers you enter.

asof.tail: Square's Free plan, tap, dip or swipe: 2.6% plus 15 cents. Type your own reader's rates.

method: What the day costs is the booth fee plus everything else the show takes: travel, parking, meals, organizer extras and a share of the tent and display you reuse.

Each piece earns its price minus its own cost and its share of card fees. The card fee per dollar of sales is the share paid by card times the percent fee plus the flat fee spread over an average customer's spend.
Pieces to break even is the day's cost divided by what each piece earns, rounded up to a whole piece. Pieces for your profit adds the profit you want to the day's cost first.
pages.example: A $150 booth fee becomes a $315.60 day once organizer extras, travel, parking, meals and a share of the display add $165.60. With an average price of $13.84, a cost of $7.30 a piece and 70% of sales by card on a 2.6% plus 15 cent reader, each piece earns $6.24. The day needs 51 pieces, $705.84 of sales, to break even, and 99 pieces, $1,370.16 of sales, to clear $300 of profit. These are the example show and products inside the Craft Fair Profit Calculator workbook.

cta.title: Plan every show of the season

faq: How many items do I need to sell to cover a booth fee?

Divide what the whole day costs by what each piece earns after its own cost and card fees, then round up. Count the whole day, not only the booth: in the example, other costs add $165.60 to a $150 booth.
Should my making time be in the cost per piece?
Yes, if you want the day to pay you for it. Leave it out and break-even only covers materials and fees.
What card fee should I use?
The one your reader charges. As of Oct 7, 2026, Square's Free plan in the US charges 2.6% plus 15 cents for tap, dip or swipe payments.
Do sales include sales tax?
No. Use prices before sales tax. Tax you collect at a show is owed to the state, not earned.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is a planning estimate based on the numbers you enter.

pages.card: A nightly rate for every month from one base rate, held at your floor.
method: Each month's season multiplier is that month's revenue last year divided by the average month. A month that brought in 31% more than average is a 1.31x month.
A month's nightly rate is your base rate times its multiplier, rounded to the dollar. If that comes out under your floor, the floor is charged instead and the month is tagged Floor.
After fee is the nightly rate minus the platform fee you type, per night. The shortest stay line adds your cleaning fee to your minimum stay in the quietest month, before any platform fee.
pages.example: Take the fictional mountain cabin in the workbook's example: a $185 base nightly rate, a $115 floor, a $120 cleaning fee and a 2-night minimum. Its last 12 months averaged $4,275 a month. July brought in $5,600, a 1.31x month, so July nights price at $242. At a 15.5% host fee a $242 July night pays out $204.49, and a 2-night November stay comes to $350 with cleaning, before platform fees. faq: How do I set seasonal prices for an Airbnb?
Compare each month of last year with your average month. That multiplier times your base rate is the month's rate, and a floor keeps a quiet month from going too low.
What is a floor rate?
The lowest nightly rate you will take, set from your own costs: cleaning, utilities, wear and your time. It is your judgment, not a computed number.
I have no booking history. What do I use?
Pick a starter curve for your kind of market, then replace it with your own months once you have a year of bookings. Starter curves are rough shapes, not market data.
Does the platform fee change my nightly rates?
Not here. The rates are what you list; the After fee column shows what each night pays out at the fee you type. Other platforms set their own fees.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is a planning estimate based on the numbers you enter.

pages.title: Debt Payoff Calculator: Avalanche vs Snowball vs Minimums | ProofNotFluff
pages.desc: Free debt payoff calculator for up to five debts. Enter each balance, APR and minimum plus an extra monthly amount to compare months to pay off and estimated interest for avalanche, snowball and minimums only.
pages.lede: Up to five debts, three ways to pay them: highest APR first, smallest balance first, or minimums only. See the months and the estimated interest for each. Free, no sign-up.
pages.card: Months to pay off and estimated interest: avalanche, snowball and minimums only.
method: Each month every balance grows by its APR divided by 12, rounded to the cent, and every minimum is paid. The minimums plus your extra amount are paid every month in both plans.

Avalanche sends the money left after minimums to the highest APR first. Snowball sends it to the smallest balance first. The order is set from today's balances, and when a debt is paid off its minimum moves to the next one. Each plan runs up to 20 years.

Minimums only pays each minimum and nothing else, with no roll-over, so each debt runs on its own schedule. If a minimum does not cover a month's interest, that balance never comes down. All interest figures are estimates.
pages.example: The workbook's example has five debts: a credit card at $4,751.76 and 24.99% APR with a $145 minimum, a store card at $854.32 and 26.99% ($40), a car loan at $10,748.15 and 7.4% ($329), a student loan at $18,658.05 and 5.5% ($205) and a personal loan at $3,142.59 and 12.9% ($112). That is $38,154.87 owed and $831 of minimums. Minimums only takes 119 months and about $11,093 of interest. At $1,100 a month, the minimums plus $269, avalanche takes 40 months and about $4,965 of interest, and snowball also takes 40 months with about $5,234. These are estimates from the Debt Payoff Tracker workbook's example, balances as of October 2026.

cta.title: Track the real balances, payment by payment
bullets: The Debt Payoff Tracker uses this same maths for Excel and Google Sheets, for up to 25 debts:
a payment log that updates each balance, both plans month by month, what to pay each debt next month, and owed over time. $2.99, instant download.

faq: What is the difference between avalanche and snowball?

Both pay every minimum and put the rest on one debt at a time. Avalanche picks the highest APR first, which usually costs less interest. Snowball picks the smallest balance first, so the first debt is gone sooner.
Why does minimums only take so long?
Part of each minimum goes to interest, and when a debt is paid off its minimum is not moved to the others. On a high APR card most of a small minimum can go to interest.
How exact are these numbers?
They are estimates. The calculator adds APR divided by 12 each month and assumes no new charges, fees or rate changes. Your lender's statements will differ.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is planning math based on the numbers you enter.

pages.title: Shipping Cost Calculator for Etsy and eBay Sellers: True Cost per Parcel | ProofNotFluff
pages.desc: Free shipping cost calculator for online sellers. Add the box, filler, tape, label paper, your packing time and the fees on the shipping you charge to the label cost, and see if your shipping charge covers it.
pages.lede: The label is only part of it. Add the box, filler, tape, your packing time and the fees on the shipping you charge, and see if what the buyer pays covers the parcel. Free, no sign-up.
pages.card: The true cost of one parcel against the shipping you charge, fees included.

asof.tail: The $0.25 per-order part of processing is charged whether or not you charge shipping, so it is not counted here.

method: The parcel cost is the label you paid plus the box or mailer, filler, tape and label paper, plus your packing minutes at your hourly rate.

Marketplaces take a fee on the shipping you charge too. For a US Etsy seller that is the 6.5% transaction fee plus 3% payment processing, 9.5% of the shipping charge. Add it to the parcel cost and you have the true cost per order.
Over or under is the shipping you charge minus that true cost. Break-even shipping is the parcel cost divided by 1 minus the fee percent, rounded up to the cent.
pages.example: A 12 oz ceramic mug ships with $4.95 charged. The label cost $9.95, the box 85 cents, filler 45 cents, tape 8 cents and label paper 6 cents, and packing takes 6 minutes at $18 an hour, $1.80. The parcel costs $13.19, $8.24 more than the buyer paid. Etsy's 9.5% on the $4.95 adds 47 cents, so each order is $8.71 short. Shipping of $14.58 would cover it. These are the sample mug's numbers in the Etsy and eBay Shipping Cost Calculator workbook.

faq: What goes into the true cost of shipping?
The label, the box or mailer, filler, tape, label paper or ink, the minutes it takes you to pack, and the marketplace fees on the shipping you charge.
Does Etsy charge fees on shipping?

Yes. For US sellers the 6.5% transaction fee and the 3% payment processing fee both apply to the shipping you charge, as of Oct 7, 2026. Processing also has a $0.25 part per order that applies with or without shipping.
Where does the label cost come from?
What you paid for the label, from your label platform or receipt. The calculator does not look up carrier rates.
What if I offer free shipping?
Type 0 for the shipping you charge. The whole parcel cost then comes out of the item price, and there is no fee on shipping.
Is this tax or financial advice?
No. It is a planning estimate based on the numbers you enter.

pages.title: Reorder Point Calculator for Small Shops: When to Reorder and How Much | ProofNotFluff
pages.desc: Free reorder point calculator for small businesses. Type daily sales, supplier lead time and safety stock to see the stock level to reorder at, how many units to order, and how many days you have left.
pages.lede: Know when to reorder before you run out. Type how fast one product sells and how long your supplier takes, and see the reorder point, how many units to order and how many days you have. Free, no sign-up.
pages.card: The stock level to reorder at, and how many units to order, for one product.
method: Reorder point = units sold per day x supplier lead time in days x (1 + safety stock). It is the stock that covers the sales you expect while an order is on its way, plus a cushion.

Order up to = units sold per day x (lead time + days between your orders) x (1 + safety stock). When you order, you order enough to get back up to this level: order up to minus on hand minus on order, rounded up to a whole unit.

The status reads Order now when on hand plus on order is at or under the reorder point, or when on hand runs out before an order could land and nothing is on order. Days until you reach the reorder point = (on hand + on order - reorder point) / units sold per day. Over 120 days of stock reads as overstocked, the workbook's default.
pages.example: Take the goat milk soap bar in the workbook's sample shop: it sells 6 a day, the supplier takes 7 days, safety stock is 20% and the shop orders every 14 days. The reorder point is 6 x 7 x 1.2 = 50.4 bars, and with 46 on hand and none on order it is time to order. Order up to is 6 x 21 x 1.2 = 151.2, so the order is 106 bars, $275.60 at $2.60 each. The shop's speckled mug sells 1.4 a day with a 21-day lead time: its reorder point is 35.28 mugs, so 48 on hand reaches it in about 9.1 days, and the next order is 24 mugs, $156. These are the sample shop's numbers in the Cash-Aware Reorder Planner workbook.

cta.title: Every product, every supplier, and the cash to pay for it
bullets: The Cash-Aware Reorder Planner uses this same maths for Excel and Google Sheets:
up to 30 products, a reorder plan in priority order, purchase orders grouped by supplier, a cash check that funds the most urgent orders first, and a dead stock list. $2.99, instant download.

faq: How do you calculate a reorder point?
Multiply the units you sell per day by your supplier's lead time in days, then add a safety stock cushion. Selling 6 a day with a 7-day lead time and 20% safety stock gives 6 x 7 x 1.2 = 50.4 units.
What is safety stock?
A cushion on top of the sales you expect while an order is on its way, written here as a percent of those sales. Raise it for a supplier that often runs late or a product whose sales jump around.
How many units should I order?
Enough to get back up to your order-up-to level: the sales you expect over the lead time plus the days until your next order, with the same cushion, minus what you have on hand and on order.
How do I find units sold per day?
Count the units sold in the last 30 days and divide by 30. A product that sold 42 units last month sells 1.4 a day.
Does this work for products with seasonal sales?
Use your recent daily sales and check again before your busy season. The workbook adds a trend adjustment that raises or lowers daily sales for the season ahead.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is a planning estimate based on the numbers you enter. Check minimum order quantities, price breaks and lead times with your supplier.
